name: Libertarianism
summary: Libertarianism treats individual liberty as the highest political value and holds that force may be used only to defend people's rights, not to make them serve others or themselves. Built on self-ownership and strong property rights, it wants a sharply limited government, free markets, free trade and free movement, low or no taxes and no redistribution. It also defends civil liberties: free speech, gun rights, legal drugs and sex work, privacy from surveillance, and non-interventionist foreign policy.
scope: Mainstream contemporary right-libertarianism, chiefly in its US form: the Libertarian Party platform, Nozick's minimal-state theory, and Cato-style libertarianism as set out by David Boaz, with Hayek and Friedman as consequentialist influences. Where the family splits (minarchism versus anarcho-capitalism, abortion), the answers follow the mainstream or record the split. It excludes left-libertarianism, libertarian socialism and Objectivism, and treats anarcho-capitalism and paleolibertarianism as strands rather than the centre.

keyFigures.name: Robert Nozick
keyFigures.role: Author of Anarchy, State, and Utopia, the leading philosophical defence of the minimal state

keyFigures.name: Friedrich Hayek
keyFigures.role: Economist and influence on libertarianism, defender of limited government and free markets

sources.usedFor: Milton Friedman's advocacy of a negative income tax as fitting limited-government and free-market thinking, and its later spread to other camps.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Libertarian Party wants a free market in medical care without government licensing or mandates, and libertarians oppose tax-funded spending on health as coercive redistribution.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Libertarians reject government price controls, which the party platform says include wages, and economists in the tradition such as Friedman argue minimum wages price low-skilled workers out of jobs.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Voluntary exchange and dispersed knowledge (Hayek) are the core economic case of the movement; planners cannot know what markets coordinate.

public-ownership.rationale: The platform says government should not compete with private enterprise; state ownership of industry is the opposite of the libertarian program.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistributive taxation is likened by Nozick to forced labor, and the party opposes any tax increase and seeks the eventual end of taxation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Robust property rights grounded in self-ownership and just acquisition are central, and the party opposes eminent domain and civil asset forfeiture.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Libertarians call for deregulation and oppose licensing and government control of business; they also oppose corporate privileges, but by separating business and state rather than by more regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The party would phase out Social Security and leave aid to private charity, and libertarian writers such as Charles Murray argue benefits discourage people from taking responsibility for themselves.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker cooperatives are acceptable if chosen voluntarily, but right-libertarians reject any norm or policy that workers should own their firms in place of private owners.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The platform commits to ending government spying on everyone and extending Fourth Amendment protection to records held by third parties.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug use is the standard victimless crime that libertarians would repeal laws against, arguing prohibition creates black markets and violence.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Libertarians support full freedom of expression; the platform says offensive language is not grounds for legal action.

strong-leader.rationale: Libertarianism is built on constitutionally limited government and against what the party calls the cult of the omnipotent state; a leader freed of checks is the danger it guards against.

state-harmful.rationale: The family is split between minarchists who want a night-watchman state and anarcho-capitalists who want none; the mainstream (Nozick, Cato, the party's support for a defensive military) still holds that a minimal state for police, courts and defense is legitimate.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform opposes laws restricting, registering or monitoring firearms and ammunition.

empower-police-military.rationale: Libertarians oppose militarism and world policing and want to abolish qualified immunity; they want a smaller military and more accountable police, not more power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The party supports the right of consenting adults to buy and sell sexual services, and prostitution bans are listed among laws libertarians oppose.

decide-locally.rationale: Libertarians favor decentralization and recognize self-determination down to secession, though their deeper preference is for individuals, not any level of government, to decide.

traditional-family.rationale: The doctrine holds government should not define or promote any kind of relationship; individual libertarians range from socially conservative right-libertarians to culturally liberal ones, so as a political claim it is neutral.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Libertarians would take government out of licensing marriage, but until then the platform says licenses should go to all consenting adults, and Boaz counts rights for gay people as progress.

abortion-legal.rationale: Libertarians are genuinely split: self-ownership arguments support choice while the right-to-life principle against initiated force supports protecting the fetus, and the party platform now takes no position.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party opposes government action that aids or attacks any religion; religion is a private, voluntary matter, though libertarians have no objection to it flourishing in civil society.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Libertarians want government to be strictly race-neutral, letting private parties respond to discrimination through boycotts, and oppose state programs to remedy group injustices.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Libertarianism is a narrow theory of government's role, not a comprehensive doctrine, and takes no stance on this question; adherents differ.

gradual-change.rationale: Hayekian libertarians value evolved institutions and incremental reform, while the party program seeks to abolish taxation and much of the state; the family is split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform holds that economic freedom demands unrestricted movement of people across borders, and the scholarship places libertarians with the left in opposing border restrictions; a paleolibertarian minority dissents.

free-trade.rationale: The party supports removing all governmental impediments to trade, and Boaz credits open markets with spreading prosperity.

nation-first.rationale: Libertarians reject both nationalism and supranational governance: they favor non-intervention and no alliances, but also free trade and migration with all; the statement's framing does not fit them.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Non-interventionism is a defining libertarian commitment; the platform opposes military aid, sanctions and regime change.

open-borders.rationale: The platform calls for unrestricted movement of people across borders, and libertarians are described as opposing border restrictions; a restrictionist minority dissents.

limit-growth.rationale: Libertarians favor economic growth through free markets and would handle environmental harm through property rights and restitution, not growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The platform rejects government control of energy prices and production and treats environmental protection as a matter of enforcing property rights, ruling out sweeping state climate programs.

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform affirms the people's right to alter, abolish or withdraw from a government that destroys liberty, while the non-aggression principle limits force to defense.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hayek's argument that knowledge is dispersed and that central planners cannot match individuals acting on their own knowledge cuts against rule by experts, though libertarians do not exalt majorities either.

central-planning.rationale: Opposition to central planning, grounded in Hayek's and Mises's knowledge and calculation arguments, is foundational.

socialized-markets.rationale: Right-libertarians defend private ownership of the means of production and voluntary capitalist exchange, not markets restricted to worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Left-libertarians and geolibertarians favor land taxes, but mainstream right-libertarians accept private appropriation of land without equality constraints and oppose taxes generally.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Bequests are voluntary transfers of justly held property, and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals.

basic-income.rationale: Most libertarians oppose state redistribution; some (left-libertarians, and Friedman's negative income tax as a welfare replacement) support versions of it, so the mainstream disagrees without strong force.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform opposes tariffs and all governmental barriers to trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is central planning in miniature and contradicts the principle that government should not direct or compete with private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Right-libertarians judge holdings by how they were acquired, not by their pattern, so they reject engineering a wider spread of property, though they oppose state ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Voluntary exchange, including wage labor and money, is for libertarians the ideal basis of human relations.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The platform calls for free-market banking and an end to inflationary policy and legal tender laws, and Javier Milei campaigned on currency competition; Friedman-style monetarists would keep a rule-bound central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-set wages and prices are the price controls the platform opposes, and libertarians oppose compulsory arbitration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Libertarians champion pluralism, open political systems and limited government, against any party monopoly on power.

democracy-best.rationale: Libertarians welcome open and democratic systems but rank constitutional limits on majority power above democracy, and public choice theory makes them skeptical of what voters produce.

direct-votes.rationale: Libertarians care more about limiting what any majority may decide than about how it decides; some back ballot initiatives for reforms such as cannabis legalization, but there is no doctrine either way.

right-to-secede.rationale: The platform recognizes the right to political self-determination including secession, which it says needs no one else's permission.

natural-rulers.rationale: All individuals are sovereign over their own lives and hold equal rights; no one has a natural title to rule others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Libertarians forbid initiating force but permit defensive force, and the platform affirms the right to abolish a destructive government, so violence is not ruled out in every case.

war-builds-character.rationale: Libertarians oppose war and militarism and favor toleration and trade over war; war expands the state.

separate-church-state.rationale: The platform opposes any government action that aids or attacks any religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws should be limited to violations of others' rights by force or fraud, and libertarianism is a political theory shared by theists and atheists alike.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists hold that all protective services could be private, and many minarchists accept private arbitration and security even while keeping a state military; the statement says only that it could be done.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform wants a military sufficient to defend against aggression, not one to police the world.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Libertarian individualism treats people as individuals, not members of ethnic groups, and the platform rejects denying rights based on ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Libertarians see voluntary exchange as mutually beneficial rather than as class exploitation; only the left-libertarian fringe sees the state as a tool of a ruling class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Justice is historical: holdings acquired by just means are just whatever pattern results, so pursuing equal outcomes requires illegitimate redistribution.

civilizational-union.rationale: Libertarians oppose building larger political units around religion or civilization and favor no entangling alliances.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Libertarians regard peaceful pursuit of one's own ends as legitimate and socially beneficial through exchange; egoists such as Rand go further, while others are neutral on its morality.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individuals are normatively primary and enforceable duties are limited to not violating others' rights; there are no enforceable positive duties to the community.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Libertarians credit markets and industrial trade with the spread of prosperity and liberty.

human-enhancement.rationale: Self-ownership means people may do as they choose with their own bodies, ruling out paternalist bans.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The platform opposes government spying and demands privacy for personal records; strong private encryption follows.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Natural-rights libertarians judge institutions by principle while consequentialist libertarians such as Friedman judge them by results; the family is split.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream libertarians work through the Libertarian Party, elections and policy advocacy; agorists who reject electoral politics are a minority strand.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Libertarians credit markets, property and the division of labour with modern prosperity and see the extended market order as civilization's achievement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hayek and the market tradition treat specialisation coordinated by prices as how dispersed knowledge is used and wealth created.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Nozick's entitlement theory rejects patterned principles like distribution by need: holdings are just if acquired and transferred justly.

production-for-use.rationale: Libertarians hold that free markets and the profit motive are the best way to meet people's needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Libertarians see profit as the outcome of voluntary exchange and entrepreneurship, and Nozick rejects the claim that market wage labour is exploitative.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Libertarians reject any concentration of coercive power, let alone a class dictatorship that abolishes property.

collective-farming.rationale: Libertarians defend private property in land and individual enterprise; voluntary communes are permitted but collectivisation is the opposite of their ideal.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Libertarians argue that free trade promotes peace and that war is driven by the state, which grows through it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nozick likens redistributive taxation to forced labor and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarians hold that law should reach only violations of others' rights by force or fraud and want victimless crimes repealed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Libertarianism is built on the rights of individuals, and its advocates treat claims of group rights as collectivism; Boaz describes individuals as the bearers of rights.

conscription.rationale: Opposition to conscription is a standard libertarian commitment, named by both Boaz and the party platform.

state-as-business.rationale: Libertarians want a minimal state limited to protecting rights, or competing private providers, not a state run by an owner-manager; neocameralism grew out of but broke with libertarianism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation by trades and communities is the opposite of libertarian individualism, though libertarians are also sceptical of party politics.

total-state.rationale: Libertarians want the state confined to protecting individual rights, with culture, education and the economy left to voluntary action.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The party platform and mainstream libertarians favour non-intervention and oppose imperialism and wars of conquest.

bound-labor.rationale: Self-ownership, the foundation of libertarianism, rules out being legally bound to land or forced to labour for another.

universal-morality.rationale: The natural-rights strand holds that rights are universal and knowable by reason, while the consequentialist strand of Hayek and Friedman makes no such claim.

single-common-good.rationale: Libertarians reject a single social goal imposed on all; individuals pursue their own ends and the state only protects the framework of rights.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The platform leaves firms to private owners and their employees, favouring voluntary bargaining without government mandates, so imposed worker or public votes on management conflict with property rights; the platform does not address board seats directly.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform says education is best provided by the free market and that parents should control all funds spent on their children's education, which supports school choice; many libertarians see vouchers only as a step short of ending public funding, and the platform does not name them.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform states that government should not incur debt, which burdens future generations without their consent, and Keynesian stimulus is contrary to the free-market view.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarians hold that property rights and free exchange are the foundation of all other liberties, and the party and Boaz argue that state economic control leads to control of everything else.

rule-by-example.rationale: Libertarians distrust the virtue of those in power and want rights secured by clear, limited law and the courts; the platform and Boaz stress constitutional limits on rulers rather than trust in their example.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Libertarians favor reason and evidence, but the family includes religious and traditionalist currents alongside secular rationalists, and the platform only defends freedom of belief; adherents are split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Libertarians mainly want to abolish welfare for everyone and oppose border limits, so they reject citizen-only benefits in principle; some accept restricting benefits as a second-best to keep borders open.

positive-liberty.rationale: Libertarians define freedom as absence of coercion and reject claims that lacking resources makes one unfree, which they see as a basis for redistribution.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Libertarians hold that law should treat individuals equally, and the platform opposes government discrimination by sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Libertarians defend free contract and the platform opposes government interference in lending and banking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Libertarians oppose government-imposed racial discrimination and defend equal individual rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Public-choice and some Rothbardian libertarians see the state as serving ruling interests, while minarchists see it as a legitimate protector of rights; the family is split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Libertarians stress individual freedom and voluntary association, so culture is a matter of private choice, and the platform favours open immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Libertarians are split: some favour proportional systems to break the two-party duopoly, others stress ballot access and limits on government over the electoral formula.

national-mission.rationale: The platform backs a non-interventionist foreign policy and opposes imposing political systems abroad.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Libertarians hold that reproductive choice belongs to the individual and state coercion violates self-ownership.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The platform opposes state abuses of force and supports accountability for officials who violate rights.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Limiting government to protecting rights through defence, courts and police is the minarchist core, set out by Nozick; anarcho-capitalists go further.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Libertarians hold that whom people marry and have children with is a private choice with no place for state or group pressure.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Individual rights and self-ownership belong equally to every person, and the platform opposes legal privilege for groups.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The platform defends freedom of religion and conscience, so the law should not limit conversion or proselytizing.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Libertarians oppose legislating morals or beliefs, so banning an act because some hold the animals sacred is rejected.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The platform backs separation of church and state, and libertarians would prefer schools to be private, but a state school should not teach doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Many libertarians ground legitimacy in individual consent, though Nozick grounds it in rights rather than agreement, so adherents are not unanimous.

trade-surplus.rationale: The party platform backs unrestricted free trade, and libertarians treat trade surpluses as a mercantilist error.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling a minority violates individual rights and the non-aggression principle that Boaz and the platform put at the centre.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The non-aggression principle, that force is justified only in defence, is the defining libertarian claim, in the party's pledge and in Boaz's essay.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Libertarians praise market competition, but they frame progress as voluntary exchange and cooperation and do not endorse struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The platform defends free association and speech without exception, so banning a party for its aims would be refused.

separated-powers.rationale: Boaz defends limited constitutional government with checks, though anarcho-capitalists reject government altogether.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Libertarians oppose redistribution and ranking claims by need, favouring equal rights and voluntary charity.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Libertarians defend free association and unions without government involvement; they generally oppose state regulation of strike and picketing as well as union privileges. The platform opposes government interference in voluntary labour relations.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Libertarians want sharply limited government and oppose a state with power over offices; lottery for public office is no libertarian aim, and Boaz stresses limited constitutional government.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Libertarians insist that rights and due process bind the state without exception; the platform opposes indefinite detention and warrantless surveillance.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform rejects government price controls, and Friedman argues in the IEP that they cause shortages.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform opposes government censorship and control of the press and the internet, and Boaz names censorship as something government must not do.

party-commands-army.rationale: Libertarians oppose party rule and want the military under constitutional limits and a narrow defence role, and they distrust standing armies.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Libertarians are split on immigration and citizenship, with open-borders and restrictionist strands since 2022; the sources give no stance on naturalization length.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The platform calls for peace with all nations and entangling alliances with none, and recognizes self-determination, so binding supranational bodies are rejected.

clerical-rule.rationale: Boaz's account stresses toleration, limited government and no state-imposed belief, which rules out rule by clergy.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The platform supports full freedom of expression and opposes government censorship in any form.

recall-officials.rationale: The platform says: we advocate initiative, referendum, recall, repeal, and oppose any effort to deny these options.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform and Boaz favor a non-interventionist foreign policy with no entangling alliances and troops brought home.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Strong property rights include the freedom to rent out property by contract, so a ban on renting would be a gross violation.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Libertarianism is tolerant of ways of life but includes strands that rank cultures by their respect for liberty; adherents are split and the core texts are silent.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The platform opposes state-mandated curricula and state schooling, so mandating creationism is rejected alongside any state-set curriculum.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Boaz and the platform oppose censorship and defend free expression and victimless-crime repeal.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Boaz stresses toleration and a diversity of lifestyles, and the creed descends from Mill's defense of experiments in living.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Individual liberty is the highest political value, and Boaz and the platform reject trading civil or political freedom for any collective goal.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property rights rest on self-ownership and are not conditional on community benefit, so the community has no claim to limit use beyond protecting others' rights.

collective-defense.rationale: The platform and Boaz favour non-intervention and peace over entangling alliances, so automatic commitments to fight are rejected.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Libertarians hold religious freedom and private property as rights, so the state may not curb or control churches.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The platform supports the right of secession, and force against an unwilling region would be aggression.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Decentralisation and the right to secede favour regions keeping their own laws and economies.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Equal individual rights and self-ownership leave no room for a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Libertarians want income tax abolished, but a flat tax is widely seen as a step toward it and Friedman and Hayek favoured simple low rates.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Limited constitutional government bound by law is core; rulers have no special privileges.

leader-cult.rationale: Opposition to the state's claims over individuals and to personal power makes leader worship alien to the platform.

land-redistribution.rationale: Libertarians hold that property rights are fundamental and oppose forced redistribution as theft.

refugee-return.rationale: Libertarians defend restoring wrongly taken property but have no stated position on a hereditary right of return; adherents split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The non-aggression principle and non-interventionist foreign policy rule out force to claim territory.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform defends freedom of religion and conscience and opposes state enforcement of faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Libertarians oppose laws that coerce peaceful personal conduct such as dress, as an infringement of individual liberty.

common-currency.rationale: Libertarians favour competing currencies and sound money over state-managed monetary systems, which opposes compulsory monetary union.

no-bailouts.rationale: Libertarians oppose bailouts and corporate subsidies, holding that firms and banks should bear their own losses.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Libertarians favour constitutionally limited government that protects individual rights against majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Libertarians hold free trade to be central and oppose tariffs and protectionism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Libertarianism rests on voluntary exchange and individual rights and opposes compelling people by state duty.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Libertarians oppose empire and intervention abroad and hold that force is only for defending rights, which rules out ruling other peoples for their own good.

patriotic-education.rationale: Libertarians want education left to families and oppose state-run schooling, and treat the state and national symbols with scepticism rather than loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Libertarians want government to be strictly race-neutral and treat people as individuals, so they oppose state-mandated or state-run racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: The platform backs free-market banking and competing currencies rather than state control of money, and libertarians oppose central planning of the money supply.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Non-interventionism and opposition to empire mean libertarians reject state projects of influence over former imperial lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Libertarians back free trade and free movement of capital and people, and urge every country to open to the world economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Libertarians hold that voluntary exchange is mutually beneficial and reject exploitation theory, so rich-country workers are not an exploiting class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarians hold that property owners may choose whom they deal with and oppose anti-discrimination law as a violation of freedom of association, though many deplore discrimination itself.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Libertarians want a limited constitutional government with individual rights written down as limits on what it may do.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rule by election rather than inheritance follows from libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices by birth conflicts with libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties; the answer is a loose inference from libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government favouring national autonomy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial claims conflict with libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Hereditary or descent-based political leadership conflicts with libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents are split between preserving history and removing honours; the ideology gives no settled position beyond libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the military conflicts with libertarian commitments to individual liberty, property rights, voluntary association and minimal government.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The platform backs free trade and open investment without government restriction.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The platform treats marriage as a private contract in which the state should not set terms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The platform calls for replacing Social Security with voluntary private provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Strong property rights, including full ownership of land with the right to sell or leave it idle, are central.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The platform backs free movement and property rights regardless of nationality.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The platform opposes government mandates on private discrimination, and libertarians judge by rights, not outcomes.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The platform and libertarian writing favour non-intervention in foreign conflicts.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Non-intervention and self-determination oppose force against another state.

corporate-influence.rationale: Libertarians blame government favours, subsidies and regulation for corporate power, so many agree money buys influence; some see it as overstated.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Libertarians oppose state controls on voluntary exchange, association and speech, which would include screening money that funds media and schools.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Libertarians oppose tax-funded benefits and state social engineering, and favour open migration, so they reject state baby bonuses.

residents-only-property.rationale: Property rights and free exchange are central, so libertarians reject government limits on who may buy land.

job-guarantee.rationale: Libertarians oppose government spending programmes and state employment as coercive redistribution; a job guarantee is a clear case.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Libertarians hold that the state's laws carry no authority in themselves, and a duty exists only toward others' rights; minarchists are more moderate.

non-intervention.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform calls for non-intervention in other nations' affairs, though some libertarians allow exceptions such as stopping atrocities.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Libertarian individualism rejects blaming people for membership of a group, so conspiracy claims against minorities are rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Libertarians hold that the state should not define or privilege any form of relationship, and see marriage as a private contract.

local-production.rationale: Libertarians favour free trade and oppose protectionism, so efficiency rather than closeness decides where goods are made.

informal-organisation.rationale: Libertarians favour voluntary, decentralised cooperation, but the Libertarian Party itself is a formal party; the question splits the family.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Libertarians distrust supranational bodies and treaties that bind domestic law, favouring national sovereignty and constitutional limits.

religious-nation.rationale: Libertarians treat identity as individual, so defining the nation by shared religion conflicts with equal individual rights.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Libertarians defend private ownership of all property, including productive property, and reject common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Libertarians oppose communism but favour peace and non-intervention over wars to defeat it; this is an inference about the mainstream.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Libertarians hold that free markets created widespread prosperity and progress.

socialized-care.rationale: Libertarians oppose tax-funded public services and redistribution, and leave care to families and voluntary arrangements.

majority-settlement.rationale: Libertarians favour free movement and oppose state social engineering of where groups live.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Libertarian property theory rests on individual homesteading and voluntary transfer, not collective historical or religious claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Libertarians oppose censoring the claim but reject it as factually false; this statement is about its truth.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform opposes laws against consensual adult sexual conduct, and Boaz stresses toleration.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Libertarians oppose censorship and state suppression of association, and the platform defends speech and assembly.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The platform and Boaz oppose state censorship and any state role in religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Libertarians oppose empire and foreign intervention and support free trade; the platform favours non-interventionism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Libertarians ground legitimacy in individual rights and consent, not religious law, and oppose political violence outside self-defence.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Many libertarians describe themselves as neither left nor right, but others see themselves as part of the right; adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Libertarians defend free labour exchange and markets and reject the Marxist critique of wage labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mainstream libertarians hold toleration and individual rights apply to people of any faith, though paleolibertarians differ.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Libertarian legitimacy rests on individual rights and consent, not on God or the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Libertarians oppose state restrictions on personal expression and religion; the platform defends religious freedom, though some accept limits on state employees.

social-market-economy.rationale: Libertarians favour free markets and oppose welfare and regulation beyond protecting rights, so they reject the mixed model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mainstream minarchist libertarians keep defence as a core function of the minimal state, though anarcho-capitalists differ.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Libertarian foreign policy favours non-interventionism and peace over entangling alliances and war.

property-franchise.rationale: Libertarianism is built on equal individual rights, which rules out wealth-based voting limits.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law with general, known rules is central to libertarian thought, as in Hayek and Nozick.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform opposes discrimination by government and holds that rights are individual.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The platform wants the state out of marriage and defends freedom of religion, so legal restriction is rejected.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Libertarians hold that wealth gained by voluntary exchange violates no rights and that the danger to liberty is state power, though they criticise crony privilege.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The platform opposes government discrimination and counts gay rights as progress, while seeing military service as voluntary.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The platform holds that government must not promote or impose religion or its absence, and tax-funded public education is itself opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Mainstream libertarians keep police and courts to protect rights; only the anarcho-capitalist strand wants them replaced by private provision.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Libertarians want voluntary charity and mutual aid to replace tax-funded welfare.

rent-control.rationale: The platform opposes government price controls, and rent caps are a standard example; libertarians answer shortages with more supply.

abolish-ip.rationale: Adherents are genuinely split: Cato-style and party libertarians often defend intellectual property as property, while Rothbardian and many anarcho-capitalist writers call it a state monopoly.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Libertarians hold that associations should be voluntary and oppose conscription and state-directed national service, so state-organised youth drill is rejected.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Libertarians treat a return on owned and invested property as legitimate and voluntary, and oppose redistribution from owners to workers.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The non-aggression principle permits force in defence of oneself and others, so a ban on lethal self-defence is rejected.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Libertarians oppose state-led nationalist veneration and cults of sacrifice, though private commemoration is fine.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Libertarianism calls for free trade and the free market and opposes state privileging of one group in commerce.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The platform favors private provision of services and opposes government ownership and monopoly, including of local utilities and hospitals.

municipal-property.rationale: Libertarians hold that productive property belongs to private owners; the platform opposes collective or government ownership.

family-wage.rationale: Wages are set by voluntary contract; the platform opposes minimum-wage and price controls, so a household-based wage standard is rejected.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The platform opposes government licensing and regulation of medicine, which includes premarket approval controls, so faster approval is the mild form of its view.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The platform defends financial privacy and sound, competing money against government control.

online-anonymity.rationale: The platform opposes government surveillance and defends privacy, which covers anonymous participation online.

person-over-state.rationale: Nozick's side constraints say individuals may not be used merely as means for others' ends, the core of the libertarian case against the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Libertarians treat spiritual life as a private matter and are split between religious and secular strands; the creed takes no stance.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Boaz describes libertarianism as individualist and opposed to collectivist treatment of people by group, racial groups included.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The platform calls for a non-interventionist foreign policy and force only in defence.

free-public-college.rationale: The platform opposes tax-funded government provision of education and libertarians treat redistributive spending as coercive.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Minarchists want the state alone to hold force, but anarcho-capitalists and the gun-rights wing defend private armed protection and militias, so the family is split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Libertarians favour voluntary contract between individuals and employers and oppose laws that compel collective bargaining, while allowing unions as voluntary associations.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The Libertarian Party opposes taxation to redistribute income, so topping up wages through the tax system is a transfer it rejects.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Libertarians want strictly limited government spending and balanced budgets, and many back constitutional limits on borrowing, though some prefer no state at all.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntary pluralism of communities, as in Nozick's framework for utopia, is a core libertarian idea; there is no imposed blueprint beyond rights.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Libertarians favour private property in resources and market prices, but reject state accounting schemes and ecosystem pricing designed by government.

sacred-nation.rationale: The nation as a sacred community overriding the individual is opposed by libertarian individualism, which makes the individual the only unit of moral concern.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The Libertarian Party opposes government subsidies to education and student loans, and debt relief is a taxpayer-funded transfer.

public-service-media.rationale: The Libertarian Party opposes government funding of media and holds that news should be left to private outlets and the market.

farm-price-support.rationale: Libertarians oppose price controls, subsidies and state credit as coercive redistribution that distorts free markets; this follows the platform's free-market stance rather than a farm-specific plank.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Libertarians are split between minimal-state defenders who keep defensive arms and non-interventionists or anarchists who favour disarmament; the sources do not settle it.

ban-fgm.rationale: The non-aggression principle forbids force against non-consenting persons, so cutting children is a rights violation the law should punish, though some libertarians stress limits on state power.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Libertarians hold that harming another's property is a rights violation to be remedied through courts and damages, and many prefer this to regulation, though Cato-style libertarians accept some rules.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Government power grounded in custom or status, rather than individual rights and consent, conflicts with the commitment to a sharply limited government of equals.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Individual liberty is the highest political value and rights may be limited only to stop harm to others, so general environmental goals do not override it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Libertarians oppose mandatory minimums as an overreach of state coercion and part of the broader criticism of the criminal justice system.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Libertarians favour free movement and oppose state compulsion, so a state-imposed language requirement conflicts with their platform on immigration.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Libertarians hold that association and contract must be voluntary, so no one may be forced to join or fund a union to hold a job; the platform's labour planks rest on this.

voter-id.rationale: Adherents split between treating ID rules as a cheap guard on election integrity and distrusting state identification and its burden on voters; the sources do not settle it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Libertarians want a state that favours no religion and leaves belief to individuals, which excludes legal precedence for any interpretation.

premarital-sex.rationale: Libertarians treat consensual adult relationships as no business of the state or of coercive social pressure; this is tolerance, not necessarily moral endorsement.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Libertarians oppose censorship and state control of communication, and a shutdown is a blanket restriction on speech and association.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Friedman proposed a negative income tax as a limited-government alternative to the welfare state, but the party platform wants welfare ended and many adherents reject any redistribution.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Libertarians oppose adding government bureaucracy and want equal legal rights without special state bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Lockean first appropriation by mixing labour with unowned resources is the standard right-libertarian account of how property arises, as in Nozick's historical theory of justice.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Libertarians reject nationalised property and central planning as coercive, so they see no reason to defend such a state.

national-church-status.rationale: The Libertarian Party platform calls for the separation of church and state and no privileges for any religion, which rules out a favoured national church.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The platform's support for the right of secession and consent of the governed leads libertarians to let local people decide their allegiance.

simple-living.rationale: Libertarians welcome trade, abundance and markets and hold that each person chooses their own way of life, so they do not set limited needs as an ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Libertarians favour free movement and oppose state limits on where people may settle, though private landowners may exclude others.

equal-conscription.rationale: Libertarians oppose conscription altogether (recorded in this audit's own missing statement at -2), so they accept the 'neither' branch, and any draft they tolerated would treat the sexes alike.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Libertarians treat the individual, not the nation, as the unit of moral concern and reject collective duties to a homeland.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The party platform opposes the drug war and insists on due process, and libertarians hold that the state may use force only against rights violators proven guilty.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The platform favours non-intervention and no entangling alliances, which rules out state action for kin abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Mainstream right-libertarians hold that homesteading gives full title with no compensation owed; left-libertarians dissent.

self-ownership.rationale: Self-ownership is the foundation of libertarian theory in the scholarship and the party's rights claims.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The party platform wants taxes cut and ultimately ended, and libertarians favour lower taxes of every kind.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Most libertarians want no tax-funded social spending, though some accept a negative income tax as better than universal welfare.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Libertarians want power limited and dispersed and oppose any leader above institutions.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The platform opposes subsidies, bailouts and corporate welfare, and libertarians oppose special privileges for connected firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Libertarians hold that religion is a private matter and government should not favour any faith, though they do not regulate how people organise.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Libertarians welcome technology and leave values to individual choice, so they neither demand nor oppose a return to ancestral values; paleolibertarians differ.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Libertarians stress individual freedom of association and equal rights, so either spouse may leave a marriage.

national-resource-control.rationale: Libertarians favour private ownership of resources and open markets and oppose nationalisation or foreign-ownership limits.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nozick's entitlement theory holds that a distribution is just if it arose through just acquisition and voluntary transfer, whatever its shape.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Libertarian Party opposes taxes on voluntary exchange as coercive, which covers a levy on currency trades.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The platform demands a sharply limited government and civil liberties, which rule out one-party control of the economy.

police-more-powers.rationale: Libertarians oppose militarism and world policing and want to abolish qualified immunity; they want a smaller military and more accountable police, not more power. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The party would phase out Social Security and leave aid to private charity, and libertarian writers such as Charles Murray argue benefits discourage people from taking responsibility for themselves. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The government should be able to conscript citizens into military service.
missingStatements.rationale: Opposition to conscription is a standard libertarian commitment, named by both Boaz and the party platform as something government must not do.

missingStatements.text: Acts between consenting adults that harm no one else should never be crimes.
missingStatements.rationale: The principle that law should reach only violations of others' rights by force or fraud, and the repeal of victimless crimes, defines libertarian criminal justice beyond any single issue.

missingStatements.text: Taxation is a form of theft or forced labor.
missingStatements.rationale: Nozick likens redistributive taxation to forced labor and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals, a claim distinct from how high taxes should be.

notes: The family is split between minarchists and anarcho-capitalists (separate catalog entries), and on abortion and, since the 2022 rise of the Mises Caucus, on immigration. Left-libertarians would answer differently on land-value tax, basic income and class. The answers follow mainstream US right-libertarianism.
